candidates.title: clear_hash_tree cannot rebuild a stored machine whose cached hash-tree files are malformed or missing: load parses and validates them first and throws
candidates.component: Emulator core: loading stored machines (hash_tree / page_hash_tree_cache / dense_hash_tree / dirty_page_tree constructors), reached through C API cm_load, Lua machine:load, JSON-RPC machine.load and the CLI --load --clear-hash-tree
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines'; O1 rebuild is on the honest operator's path)
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::machine (m_ht constructed at line ~313, clear_hash_tree() only at line ~326 after construction); src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::hash_tree (lines 979-1005: 'inconsistent amount of sparse hash tree nodes', 'inconsistent sparse hash tree nodes'); src/page-hash-tree-cache.hpp constructor (file tag mismatch, check_metadata: borrowed entry, LRU size/links, duplicate page address); src/os-mapped-memory.cpp (exact backing length / missing file); src/memory-address-range.cpp lines 72-75 (dht/dpt mapped with exact length; a missing dht/dpt is only recreated when shared); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp prepare_ar_backing_store
candidates.description: O1 requires an adopter to 'rebuild the cached hash-tree data from the contents when loading it'. The only documented rebuild is runtime option clear_hash_tree (CLI --clear-hash-tree). But the machine constructor first builds the hash tree and the address ranges from the cached files (hash_tree.sht, hash_tree.phtc, every *.dht and *.dpt) and validates them structurally, and only afterwards calls clear_hash_tree(). Any malformed cached data therefore makes the load throw before the rebuild runs: a sparse-tree node whose left/right/parent/log2_size differ from the layout derived from the config, a phtc with an unknown tag, a set borrowed flag, an inconsistent LRU, a truncated or missing sht/phtc, a truncated dpt/dht, or (without sharing) a missing dht. None of this data is part of the state hash or of any valid-template condition (THREAT_MODEL section 2 'Cached hash-tree data ... is outside the state hash'; section 4 'A snapshot's cached hash-tree data is not part of any valid-template condition'), so a directory whose contents meet every valid-template condition cannot be adopted through the documented rebuild. Everything that is cleared anyway is still parsed and trusted for structure. (Manual workaround that is not documented: zero the sht, zero the phtc tag, zero byte 0 of each dpt, which makes the constructors re-initialize them.)
candidates.trigger: Whoever publishes or hands over the stored template directory (application developer, a mirror, a peer validator, a corrupted transfer) ships it with malformed or missing cached hash-tree files. The honest operator follows O1 and loads it with clear_hash_tree=true (cartesi-machine --load=DIR --clear-hash-tree, machine:load(dir,{clear_hash_tree=true}), JSON-RPC machine.load, or the PRT player's new_machine/new_stored_player).
candidates.reachability: No guest or input involvement: it is reached on the first load of any adopted template whose cached files are malformed. The template's hashed contents can be exactly the ones committed on-chain (a valid template).

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. Section 8 excludes 'Defects triggered only by loading a snapshot that the emulator did not write and that does not meet the conditions of a valid template' — here the snapshot meets them, because 'A snapshot's cached hash-tree data is not part of any valid-template condition' (section 4). It also excludes 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data ... to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)' — here the defect happens during the rebuild itself. Section 5: 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too ... the emulator must make them possible to follow. A defect that defeats the rebuild itself ... is not excused by them.'
rating_steps.2_role: Loading a stored machine: AUDIT.md table puts 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines' in the Honest operator role. Section 2 'Honest operator's path: Obtaining its valid template. For a template the operator did not produce, this includes rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1).'
rating_steps.3_high_medium: No High case fits (not an unreachable state, not data the operator may decline in the sense of logs/proofs). The Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly ... in an uncommon host setup that the manual documents, or while cleaning up after a stop' does not fit: the host setup is ordinary and no stop is involved.
rating_steps.4_critical: Violates O1 as it binds the emulator ('the emulator must make them possible to follow') on the honest operator's path (obtaining its valid template), and section 4/8: 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory.' The honest operator cannot obtain the template it must defend -> Completeness failure ('cannot produce a proof ... or cannot respond in time'). Literal reading: Critical.
rating_steps.5_low: Alternative reading: if 'make the rebuild possible' only requires the rebuild to work on cached data of the emulator's own format, and a loud refusal is acceptable because the operator can obtain the template elsewhere, this is a Low robustness defect. The deciding fact is whether a snapshot whose contents meet every valid-template condition must be adoptable regardless of its cached data (section 4 wording says it must not 'crash the honest operator' and is 'defended only after that data is rebuilt').

candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (literal reading of O1 'the emulator must make them possible to follow'); Low under the narrower reading
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 assumes the honest operator obtains its valid template. Whoever distributes the template directory can make every honest operator that follows O1 fail to load it, so no honest claim is posted or defended and any claim can win (completeness).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O1/exp/loadfail.lua on a copy of bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine stored with SHARING_ALL (true root 0x428a6b...). With clear_hash_tree=true, both SHARING_NONE and SHARING_ALL: sht node 2 left index changed -> 'inconsistent sparse hash tree nodes'; phtc LRU size 2^40 -> 'corrupted page hash-tree cache: invalid LRU link'; phtc entry 0 borrowed flag -> 'corrupted page hash-tree cache: borrowed entry'; phtc tag 0x1234 -> 'file tag mismatch'; sht truncated to 64 bytes or missing, phtc missing, RAM dpt truncated -> backing length / open errors; RAM dht missing -> load fails without sharing (rebuilt OK with SHARING_ALL). In contrast, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O1/exp/corrupt.lua shows that cached hashes (all dht bytes, all sht hash fields, all phtc payloads, all dpt bytes) are fully neutralized by clear_hash_tree as long as the structure fields are intact.
candidates.test_idea: Store the baremetal template with SHARING_ALL, record its rebuilt root, overwrite the left index of sparse node 2 in hash_tree.sht (offset 128, int64) and the phtc tag; then pcall(cartesi.machine, dir, {clear_hash_tree=true}) and require that it loads and get_root_hash() equals the recorded root. Exits 1 today (load throws).

candidates.title: config.json hash_tree.phtc_size of an adopted template (outside the hashed state) survives clear_hash_tree and sets the memory and time of loading and rebuilding without bound, and is inherited by every later store and clone
candidates.component: Emulator core: loading stored machines (page_hash_tree_cache sized from machine_config.hash_tree.phtc_size read from config.json); machine::store/clone_stored propagate the value
candidates.role: Honest operator (loading, storing and cloning machines)
candidates.location: src/machine-config.cpp machine_config::load (hash_tree config taken from config.json; adjust_ht_backing_store_config changes only filenames/shared/create); src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::hash_tree line ~980 (page cache built with config.phtc_size); src/page-hash-tree-cache.hpp constructor (m_map.reserve(num_entries); uninitialized file -> placement-new and clear_hash_tree of every payload) and clear() (writes every payload); src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::clear; src/machine.cpp machine::store / clone_stored (config.json re-written/cloned with the same phtc_size)
candidates.description: The capacity of the page hash-tree cache comes from hash_tree.phtc_size in the stored config.json, which is neither in the hashed state nor reset by clear_hash_tree, and which the runtime configuration cannot override. The only checks are that it is non-zero, that the layout arithmetic does not overflow ptrdiff_t, and that hash_tree.phtc has exactly the matching length, which a sparse file satisfies at no disk cost. Loading then reserves a map of phtc_size entries, initializes every entry of an uninitialized cache, and clear_hash_tree() (the O1 rebuild) writes the 4 KiB page and the 8 KiB pristine page tree of every entry. Host memory and CPU of the load therefore grow linearly with a number chosen by whoever produced the directory, independent of the machine's size (about 10.5 KB of resident memory per entry measured). phtc_size of about 2^21 needs about 22 GB and kills a 16 GB host; larger values exhaust any host. Because store() and clone_stored() copy the config, every machine the operator later stores, clones or forks from the template (PRT epoch machine, machine-cache entries, pair/agreed/revert backups, spawned servers) carries the same capacity, multiplying the cost; with SHARING_ALL the cache file is also written out in full, consuming disk per directory.
candidates.trigger: Whoever distributes the template directory sets "phtc_size" in config.json and supplies a sparse hash_tree.phtc of the matching length (GNU tar --sparse keeps it small). The honest operator adopts it following O1 (any load path, with or without clear_hash_tree).
candidates.reachability: First load of the adopted template; the hashed contents can be exactly the on-chain committed template, so the snapshot meets every valid-template condition.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded: the snapshot meets the valid-template conditions (phtc_size is not one of them), and the defect does not need cached data to survive without a rebuild; it bites during the rebuild. Section 8: 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory.'
rating_steps.2_role: Loading, storing and cloning machines are Honest operator (AUDIT.md table).
rating_steps.3_high_medium: If one reads it as a constant-factor cost increase within the deployment's sizing, High ('A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor'); but the factor is not constant, it is chosen freely by the directory's producer, so that case does not fit.
rating_steps.4_critical: R12: 'storing, loading, cloning or syncing a machine' must have a worst case 'bounded and at most linear in ... the bytes it covers'; here it is unbounded in a value outside the state. Section 4: 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator'; an OOM kill on adoption is such a crash, on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template'). Critical.
rating_steps.5_low: If triage holds that a template distributor that sabotages the directory is equivalent to a non-valid template, Low; the deciding fact is that phtc_size lives outside every valid-template condition and outside the hashed state.

candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (R12 unbounded load cost / crash of the honest operator from data outside the hashed state); High if read as a sizing-bounded cost multiplier
candidates.threat_to_goal: Every honest operator adopting the published template runs out of memory (or disk, with sharing) while loading or rebuilding it, so it cannot compute claims (completeness). Even sub-fatal values multiply the memory of each of the many machine instances a validator keeps.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O1/exp/mk.sh and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O1/exp/rss.lua on the baremetal template (64 MiB RAM): phtc_size 4096 (default, 50 MB sparse phtc) -> VmHWM 139720 kB, 0.11 s CPU for load+clear+get_root_hash; phtc_size 32768 (404 MB sparse phtc, 0 blocks on disk) -> VmHWM 485280 kB, 0.39 s CPU; same root hash. Linear, ~10.5 KB per entry, unrelated to the machine's bytes. Did not run a value that would exhaust the shared host.
candidates.test_idea: Copy a stored template, set phtc_size to 2^16 in config.json and truncate hash_tree.phtc to the matching length; load with clear_hash_tree in a child process under a fixed RLIMIT_AS (e.g. 2x the RSS of the default load) and require that the load succeeds and the root hash matches (or that the load ignores/clamps the stored capacity). Fails today (allocation failure / exceeds limit).

candidates.title: PRT player adopts the template by comparing the on-chain template hash with a root read from the cached hash tree (store_first_epoch_checkpoint loads without clear_hash_tree), so a valid template with stale cached data is refused forever
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint and assert_rolling_template, crisium.lua epoch-0 check, prt-demo.lua orchestration)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint lines 2743-2776 (cartesi.machine(temporary_directory) without {clear_hash_tree=true}; template_hash = machine:get_root_hash(); assert_rolling_template's get_node_hash(UARCH_STATE...) also on the cached tree; epoch.json initial/final_state_hash = template_hash); doc/recipes/crisium.lua line 236 (assert(manifest.final_state_hash:lower() == template_hash, "epoch 0's checkpoint is not the template")); doc/recipes/prt.lua new_stored_player lines 3206-3218 (only afterwards clones and rebuilds, comparing the rebuilt root with the cached one from the manifest); prt-demo.lua lines 76 and 131
candidates.description: O1: the adopter 'rebuilds the cached hash-tree data from the contents when loading it, and only then compares the root hash with the on-chain commitment.' The player's template adoption does the opposite. store_first_epoch_checkpoint clones the template directory, loads the clone with the default runtime configuration (no clear_hash_tree), checks the rolling-template conditions (including the pristine-uarch node via get_node_hash) on that cached tree, and records machine:get_root_hash(), a root read from the cached hash-tree data, as initial_state_hash/final_state_hash of epoch.json. crisium.lua then compares this cached root with the application's on-chain getTemplateHash. The rebuild comes only later in new_stored_player, which checks the rebuilt root against the cached one. Consequences: (a) a template whose contents match the on-chain commitment but whose cached data is stale or garbage gets a wrong hash in epoch.json, crisium fails its assertion on every relaunch (the checkpoint already exists, so store_first_epoch_checkpoint returns early and never fixes it), and the honest and sentinel players never defend epoch 0 or any later epoch; (b) the valid-template checks run on cached data instead of rebuilt data. Every other adoption path (prt.new_machine, vg.lua, get_stored_root_hash) uses clear_hash_tree, so this one is inconsistent with the rest.
candidates.trigger: The orchestrator (prt-demo.lua, or anyone deploying the player per the recipe) passes a template directory that the operator did not produce and whose cached hash-tree data does not match its contents.
candidates.reachability: Reached on every first start of the player on such a template; no guest action is needed.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. The template's contents meet the valid-template conditions; the defect is that the tool skips the rebuild O1 demands, which section 5 does not excuse: 'The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them.' The exclusion of 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data ... to survive its adoption without a rebuild' is about operators who skip the rebuild; here the shipped reference implementation is the one that skips it.
rating_steps.2_role: The PRT player is Support per AUDIT.md. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator.'
rating_steps.3_high_medium: In the honest-operator role it would be Critical (step 4): it violates O1 on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template ... includes rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)') and causes a completeness failure ('cannot respond in time'). Hence Medium for the Support component: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium.'
rating_steps.4_critical: Not applicable (support components are capped at Medium).

candidates.threat_to_goal: If a production node copied this reference adoption, a valid template with stale cached data would leave the honest operator unable to start (completeness), and its template checks would trust unchecked cached data, against O1's order 'rebuild, then compare'.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O1/exp/checkpoint.lua: stored the baremetal template with SHARING_ALL (rebuilt root 0x428a6bb8...), overwrote one cached RAM dense-tree node (offset 96 of 0000000080000000-4000000.dht) and marked the RAM dirty-page tree clean (byte 0 = 1, the rest 0); contents unchanged. prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint(template, {log2_mcycles_per_period=10}, out) succeeded and wrote final_state_hash 0x0f8f9593...3f82 in epoch.json, while cartesi-machine --load=template --clear-hash-tree --initial-hash prints 0x428a6bb8...ac75 (and without --clear-hash-tree prints 0x0f8f...). crisium.lua would compare 0x0f8f... with the on-chain template hash 0x428a... and abort.
candidates.test_idea: Build the stale-cache template as above; call prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint and prt.load_epoch_checkpoint; require that manifest.final_state_hash equals the root rebuilt with clear_hash_tree (0x428a...). Exits 1 today.

not_covered: Did not audit every guest-visible use of the hot TLB / penumbra after load beyond confirming init_hot_tlb_contents resets it and shadow_tlb_verify_slot re-verifies shadow slots.
Did not test the JSON-RPC machine.load path with corrupted caches directly (only the Lua local path; the PRT demo exercises JSON-RPC load with clear_hash_tree).
Did not test replace_memory_range / swap with a replacement image that ships its own stale .dht/.dpt (not a stored-machine adoption, outside O1 strictly).

Did not check whether log producers or collect_* that use skip_hash_tree_update can run right after an API clear_hash_tree() without a prior update (looked only at get_root_hash/get_node_hash/get_proof).
Did not inspect Windows/non-mmap code paths of os::mapped_memory::clear and file mapping.
Did not examine machine-guest-tools or Dave contracts (no O1 surface there) nor the Rust/other nodes (out of scope).
Did not explore sharing=config loads of an adopted template whose config.json sets shared=true (writes to the template's own files; O2 territory).

Valid-template conditions that loading does not enforce in general (register WARL legality, hash function vs deployment) were only reasoned about: registers are hashed and covered by the on-chain comparison, so a non-valid committed template is out of scope; PMA table consistency with config.json is checked (512 bytes, with the zero sentinel always inside for reproducible machines: at most 24 PMAs).
